spots.name: Market Church
spots.summary: The Market Church is the main Lutheran church in Hanover, Germany. Built in the 14th century, it was referred to in 1342 as the church of Saints James and George in dedication to Saint James the Elder and Saint George.

spots.name: Kröpcke
spots.summary: Kröpcke is the central square of the city of Hanover in Germany. The square is situated at the five-way crossroads of Georgstraße, and Karmarschstraße, Bahnhofstraße and Rathenaustraße.

spots.name: Hannover Hauptbahnhof
spots.summary: Hannover Hauptbahnhof is the main railway station for the city of Hanover in Lower Saxony, Germany. The railway junction is one of the 21 stations listed as a railway Category 1 station by DB InfraGO.

spots.name: Herrenhausen Gardens
spots.summary: The Herrenhausen Gardens of Herrenhausen Palace are located in Herrenhausen, an urban district of Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. Dating to the era of the prince-electors of Hanover and kings of Hanover, they comprise Great Garden, Hill Garden, Georgen Garden and Guelf Garden.

spots.name: New Town Hall
spots.summary: The New Town Hall is a town hall in Hanover, Germany. It opened on 20 June 1913 after construction lasting 12 years.

spots.name: Maschsee
spots.summary: The Masch Lake is an artificial lake situated south of the city centre of Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. Covering an area of 78 hectares, it is the largest body of water within Hanover and a popular recreation area as well as venue for numerous water sports.

spots.name: Leineschloss
spots.summary: The Leine Palace, situated on the Leine in Hanover, Germany, is a former residence of the Hanoverian dukes, electors and kings. It is now the seat of the parliament of Lower Saxony.

spots.name: Aegidienkirche

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aegidien Church, after Saint Giles to whom the church was dedicated, is a war memorial in Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. The church dates from 1347, when it replaced an older Romanesque church dating to 1163. This in turn replaced an even earlier chapel.

spots.name: Herrenhausen Palace

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Herrenhausen Palace is a former royal summer residence of the House of Hanover in the Herrenhausen district of the German city of Hanover. It is the centrepiece of Herrenhausen Gardens. Sophia of Hanover oversaw the development of the estate in the late 1600s.

spots.name: Old Town Hall
spots.summary: The Old Town Hall is a former, and the first, town hall in Hanover, Germany. Originally built in the old city district in 1410, replaced by the New Town Hall in 1913, and extensively restored in 1953 and 1964 after heavy bomb damage in World War II, it is the oldest secular building in the city.

spots.name: Ihme-Zentrum
spots.summary: The Ihme Centre is a residential, business and former shopping centre in Hanover between the Linden and Calenberger Neustadt quarters. It is located on the western bank of the Ihme river.

spots.name: Sprengel Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Sprengel Museum is a museum of modern art in Hanover, Lower Saxony, holding one of the most significant collections of modern art in Germany. It is located in a building situated adjacent to the Masch Lake approximately 150 metres (490 ft) south of the state museum.

photo.author: The original uploader was Axel Hindemith at German Wikipedia.

spots.name: Opera House
spots.summary: Hanover State Opera is a German opera company based in Hanover, the state capital of Lower Saxony. The company is resident in the Hanover Opera House, and is part of a publicly-funded umbrella performing arts organisation called Hanover State Theatre of Lower Saxony, or simply Hanover State Theatre.

spots.name: Reitwallstraße
spots.summary: The Reitwallstraße is a street in Hanover, Germany. Situated near the pedestrianised Stone Gate Square, it is part of the red-light district bounded by Reuterstraße, Goethestraße, Reitwallstraße and Am Marstall, crossed by Scholvinstraße. It is known for strip clubs and prostitution in Germany.

spots.name: Hanover Zoo
spots.summary: Hanover Zoo is located in the Mitte borough of Hanover, Germany. The zoo was established on 4 May 1865, and comprises an area of 22 hectares. It contains about 3,414 animals in 237 species, which are cared for by more than 400 employees in the summer season.

photo.author: Joachim Meyer - User: (WT-shared) HaJo at wts wikivoyage

spots.name: Museum August Kestner

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The August Kestner Museum, previously Kestner-Museum, is a museum in Hanover, Germany. Founded in 1889, the museum was renamed in December 2007 to avoid confusion with the Kestnergesellschaft, a local art gallery.

spots.name: Kestnergesellschaft

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Kestner Gesellschaft is an art institution in Hanover, Germany, founded in 1916 to promote the arts. It is one of the largest art associations in Germany. The halls of the Goseriedebad, which once housed an indoor swimming pool, regularly host extensive group and solo exhibitions.

spots.name: Kreuzkirche, Hanover

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Holy Cross is a Lutheran church in the centre of Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. A Gothic hall church, it is one of three churches in Hanover's old town – the other two being Market Church and Aegidien Church, although the latter is now a war memorial.

spots.name: Eilenriede
spots.summary: The Eilenriede is a 640-hectare (1,600-acre) municipal forest in Hanover, Germany. It is the largest urban city forest in Germany, one of the largest in Europe, and is nearly twice the size of Central Park in New York.

spots.name: Neustädter Kirche, Hanover

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The New Town Church is a main Lutheran parish church in Hanover, Germany. Its official name is St. John's Church of the court and city in the New Town at Hanover.

spots.name: Landesmuseum Hannover

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Lower Saxon State Museum Hanover is the state museum of Lower Saxony in Hanover, Germany. Situated adjacent to the New Town Hall, the museum comprises the state gallery, featuring paintings and sculptures from the Middle Ages to the 20th century, and departments of archaeology, natural history and ethnology.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Basilica St. Clemens

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St. Clement's Basilica is the main Roman Catholic church in the city of Hanover. It is dedicated to Saint Clement of Rome. It is part of the parish of St. Heinrich and belongs to the Diocese of Hildesheim.

spots.name: Historisches Museum Hannover

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Hanover Historical Museum is an historical museum situated in Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. The museum was founded in 1903 as the Homeland Museum of the City of Hanover. Its collections are related to the history of the city, the history of the House of Guelf, and of the state of Lower Saxony.

spots.name: Waterloo Column
spots.summary: The Waterloo Column is a victory column commemorating the Battle of Waterloo. It is situated in Hanover, the capital of the German state of Lower Saxony. Built from 1825 to 1832, it was designed by Georg Ludwig Friedrich Laves who had been the Hanover court architect since 1814.

spots.name: Aegidientorplatz
spots.summary: Aegidien Gate Square is a busy square known colloquially as Aegi in Hanover, Germany. Located above a subway station of the same name, the square was named for the Aegidien Gate, one of the city gates of medieval Hanover. While the gate was removed in 1780, the square is still named after it.

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.name: Memorial to the murdered Jews of Hanover
spots.summary: The Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Hanover is located in Hanover, Germany, on Opernplatz, one of the city's central squares. It was designed by the Italian artist Michelangelo Pistoletto and erected in 1994 on the initiative of the Memoriam Association and financed through individual donations.
spots.wikipediaTitle: Memorial to the murdered Jews of Hanover

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Wilhelm Busch Museum

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: The Wilhelm Busch Museum is a museum in Hanover, Lower Saxony, Germany. It features the world's largest collection of works by Wilhelm Busch, as well as contemporary comic art, illustrations and drawings.

spots.name: Hildesheimer Straße
spots.summary: Hildesheimer Straße is a main road in Hanover and the neighbouring town of Laatzen, Germany. It is about 14 kilometers long and used by B Line of Hanover Stadtbahn. Connecting central Hanover to the districts in the south, it is one of Hanover's most important and most-used roads.

spots.name: Wangenheim Palace
spots.summary: Wangenheim Palace is a building in the Mitte district of Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. From 1863 to 1913, it was the town hall and seat of the city's administration. Today it is the seat of the Lower Saxon Ministry of Economic Affairs.

spots.name: Stadthalle Hannover
spots.summary: The Stadthalle Hannover is a concert hall and event venue in Hanover, the capital of Lower Saxony, Germany. The large hall is called Kuppelsaal, after its dome. The hall was opened in 1914. It is the largest hall for classical music in Germany, seating 3,600.

spots.name: Broyhan House
spots.summary: Broyhan House is a residential and commercial building constructed in 1576 in Hanover's historic old town. It is the second-oldest preserved half-timbered building in Hanover, and stands on the cellar walls of an earlier building dating to the 14th century.

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.name: Gartenfriedhof
spots.summary: The Garden Cemetery is a cemetery in Hanover, Germany. It was created in 1741 and is located by the Garden Church built in 1749. The cemetery and the church are both named after the garden parish outside the former parish city walls in front of Aegidien Gate.

spots.name: Berggarten
spots.summary: The Hill Garden is a historic botanical garden, one of the gardens of the Herrenhäuser Gärten, around the residence Herrenhäuser Schloss in Herrenhausen, now part of Hanover, Lower Saxony, Germany.

spots.name: German National Library of Science and Technology
spots.summary: The German National Library of Science and Technology, abbreviated TIB, is the national library of the Federal Republic of Germany for all fields of engineering, technology, and the natural sciences. It is jointly funded by the Federal Ministry of Education and Research (BMBF) and the 16 German states.
spots.wikipediaTitle: German National Library of Science and Technology

spots.name: Old Jewish Cemetery, Hanover
spots.summary: The Old Jewish Cemetery on the Oberstrasse is a Jewish cemetery in Hanover. Located on a hill in the city's Nordstadt district, it is the oldest extant Jewish cemetery in Northern Germany. The cemetery contains about 700 graves and was in use from circa 1550 until 1864.

spots.name: Hanover War Cemetery
spots.summary: Hanover War Cemetery is a military cemetery owned by the Commonwealth War Graves Commission (CWGC). It is located in the city of Seelze, immediately adjacent to the city of Hanover, and contains predominantly Commonwealth burials of World War II.

spots.name: Georgengarten
spots.summary: The Georgengarten is a landscape garden in the northwestern borough of Herrenhausen of the German city Hanover. It is a part of Herrenhausen Gardens.

spots.name: The Nanas
spots.summary: Created by Niki de Saint Phalle in 1974, these three colorful, oversized sculptures on the banks of the Leine represent the beginning of Hanover's Sculpture Mile. While initially controversial, they are now a central landmark of the city and host Germany's oldest flea market every Saturday.

spots.name: Sea Life

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Hanover Aquarium, has an array of fish and also a rain forest inside. It is open from 10:00 daily. Tickets are usually available at a discount rate online: https://www.visitsealife.com/hannover/en/tickets/

spots.name: List
spots.summary: A residential area not so far from the Central Station. This area is popular among students. It has a nice pedestrian area "Lister Meile" with some small and interesting shops.

spots.name: University of Hanover
spots.summary: The main building was the winter palace of the Kings of Hanover. The summer palace was in the Great Garden complex. However, it was destroyed during the World War II. Now only one wall remains.

spots.name: Great Garden of Herrenhausen
spots.summary: The world-famous baroque gardens of Herrenhausen were created in the 17th century to copy the Versailles Garden in France. A must see! Even in the winter one can still see its beauty, but it reaches its best at the end of spring until end of summer. There is also a glimmering cave decorated by Niki de Saint Phalle. The Berggarten, a botanical garden, is also very beautiful.

photo.author: This image is a work by Wikipedia and Wikimedia Commons user C.Suthorn. When reu

spots.name: City park
spots.summary: This is worth visiting on a nice sunny day. Good place to relax with a good book and a perfect place to escape the city centre.

spots.name: 11A
spots.summary: A smaller cosy restaurant and wine bar in same building. Pretty large portions with decent price of fusion food (seafood, meat, vegetarian etc). Some seats inside, but most tables outside. Good menu and daily specials. Please book a table in advance on warm evenings, because it is popular among locals. You can also wait for a table in the wine bar, next to green park.

spots.name: Bistro Tomate

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Small bistro. There are indoor and outdoor spaces. The equipment is not the newest but it is tidy and gives the shop a certain charm. Customers are warmly welcomed. You have a direct view of the kitchen and can see what is being done. After you have ordered the food at the counter, you can take it with you or it will be brought to your seat.

spots.name: Restaurant "Alexander

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great schnitzel. Authentic German food. There's a large menu to choose from, and an English one is available if needed. The beer is good, with a decent selection. There's also a broader drink menu as well as desserts. Great hospitality, very pleasant attitude from the host and staff.

spots.name: Hey Ferry

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Fresh ingredients and sauces and freshly fried falafels, really crispy and tasty. Also offers döner kabab. If you're vegan they will take care not to use any dairy products. The staff is friendly and helpful and you can even try before you buy. You can sit in or take away.

spots.name: Café Mezzo

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Lister Meile 4. Normally crowded with students during lunch and dinner time. Reservations should be considered if planning to come during this time. Service can be slow sometime, but they offer a wide range of student menus with reasonable prices.

spots.name: Das kleine Museum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A corner restaurant-pub with large portions of excellent German, French, and Moroccan inspired food. Run by the owner, the staff are warm and welcoming. The decorations are true to its name, replete with stuffed crocodiles on the roof.

spots.name: Gaststätte Kaiser

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Traditional German cuisine of Lower Saxony in an atmospheric restaurant; comprehensive whiskey list. Located near the university, this is a favourite of visiting professors and researchers. The owner also rents rooms upstairs.

spots.name: Basil

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: Dining in a high ceiling, brick domed room creating a medieval appearance whilst at the same time being contemporary and modern. The menu is fresh and changes every 3 weeks to keep it that way. International meals.

spots.name: Urfa Class

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Turkish breakfast is fantastic here, vegetarian option with Menemen (scrambled eggs with tomatoes) are also available. Great döner kebab. Rare restaurant that cooks with charcoal. The staff is very attentive.

spots.name: Kebap 63

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Great kebab with large portions. The vegetarian option is also great. Many different ingredients, including grilled vegetables. They customize your food according to your wish. Free tea is always available.

spots.name: Mövenpick

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The best place to come for the all-you-can-eat-and-drink breakfast. But not for late sleepers as the breakfast ends at 11:30. Try the ice cream, a bit expensive but definitely worth the price.

spots.name: Riccardo Berardino Pizzeria

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: It has a history of over 40 years. The pizza is well filled, a little fried and therefore very juicy. The stuffed pizza is always worth a detour. Crispy, fluffy dough, aromatic cheese.
